question: Upper GI endoscopy is indicated in a child with known portal hypertension (for variceal screening), unexplained upper GI bleeding, or suspected oesophageal varices — and is a key diagnostic and therapeutic procedure in paediatric hepatobiliary disease.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Upper GI endoscopy is BOTH diagnostic and therapeutic in portal hypertension. Children with EHPVO or cirrhosis should undergo screening endoscopy for varices; when found, prophylactic endoscopic variceal ligation (EVL) is performed. OGD is also essential for diagnosing coeliac disease (duodenal biopsy), peptic ulcer disease, and foreign body retrieval.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Indications for upper GI endoscopy (OGD) in children include: (1) upper GI bleeding (haematemesis/melaena) — both diagnostic and therapeutic (variceal ligation, sclerotherapy, clipping), (2) variceal surveillance in portal hypertension, (3) suspected coeliac disease (duodenal biopsy for Marsh grading), (4) peptic ulcer disease/H. pylori testing, (5) ingested foreign body retrieval, (6) caustic ingestion assessment. Contraindications include haemodynamic instability and suspected perforation.
